content: Silver sulfadiazine is a sulfa-based medication prescribed to prevent and treat infections in secondand third-degree burns. It works by eliminating a broad spectrum of bacteria. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Silver sulfadiazine is available as a cream and is typically applied once or twice daily. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as directed. Do not use more or less of it, or apply it more frequently than prescribed. Avoid using this medication on infants under 2 months of age. Continue using silver sulfadiazine until your doctor advises you to stop, ensuring the burn has healed sufficiently to prevent infection. Gently wash the burned area daily to remove dead skin. If the burn becomes infected or the infection worsens, contact your doctor immediately. Before applying the cream, clean the burned area and remove any dead or burned skin. Always wear sterile, disposable gloves when applying the medication. Cover the cleaned burn with a layer of cream approximately 1/16 inch thick. Ensure the burned area remains covered with the cream at all times, reapplying as needed to any uncovered areas. Before using silver sulfadiazine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to this medication, sulfa drugs, or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are taking, including vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while using this medication, contact your doctor immediately. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Silver sulfadiazine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following mild symptoms, especially if they persist or worsen: pain, burning, or itching. If you experience severe side effects, such as unusual bleeding or bruising, fever, sore throat, yellowing of the skin or eyes, blood in the urine, aching joints, unusual weakness or tiredness, or a skin rash, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Silver sulfadiazine is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not ingest it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. Do not share this medication with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Notify your doctor if your skin condition worsens or does not improve.
